# 2.1.6 Cross Product

The **cross product**, also called the outer product between vectors, is a fundamental operation in linear algebra. Similar to dot products and most elementwise operations, we need both the vectors to be of the same length to perform this operation. On performing this operation on two vectors, we get a matrix.

\

**Definition 2.1.6** (Cross Product). Let $\mathbf{u}, \mathbf{v} \in \mathbb{R}^d$ be column vectors. Then the **cross product** (also called the **outer product**) of $\mathbf{u}$ and $\mathbf{v}$ is the matrix:
$$
\mathbf{u} \otimes \mathbf{v} = \mathbf{u} \mathbf{v}^T \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d}
$$
That is, each entry of the resulting matrix is the product of a component from $\mathbf{u}$ and a component from $\mathbf{v}$:
$$
(\mathbf{u} \otimes \mathbf{v})_{ij} = u_i v_j
$$
\
**Example 2.1.6**
Let 
$$
\mathbf{u} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}, \quad 
\mathbf{v} = \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix}
$$

Then,
$$
\mathbf{u} \otimes \mathbf{v} = \mathbf{u} \mathbf{v}^T = 
\begin{bmatrix} 
1 \cdot 3 & 1 \cdot 4 \\
2 \cdot 3 & 2 \cdot 4
\end{bmatrix}
= 
\begin{bmatrix}
3 & 4 \\
6 & 8
\end{bmatrix} \in \mathbb{R}^{2 \times 2}
$$
